what: Plate recognisers compared on this deployment's own footage (licensed Mumbai signal-queue clip, 2560x1440). Plate strings are not reproduced here.

crop_level.set: 21 plate crops read by eye, plus 2 a person could not read; crops as the pipeline hands them to OCR
crop_level.note: The Indian model's reads on the 2 unreadable crops scored 0.725 and 0.805, under the 0.82 bar a single-frame read must clear to publish.
crop_level.preprocessing: Padded as the weights' published inference script pads (black, before scaling): 6/21 exact. Padded as PaddleOCR's resize_norm_img pads in training (grey, after): 17/21.

port_parity: PyTorch port vs PaddlePaddle forward pass on the 23 crops: max probability difference 7.45e-06, same text 23/23 (tools/bench/ocr_compare.py --parity).

clip_level.clip: OWN-MUM-QUEUE, 57 s, 1,716 frames, the full production pipeline (tools/demo/analyse_own_feed.py)

published_marks_checked_by_eye.method: each published mark's largest vehicle box, plate re-detected and enlarged; a mark counts only where the crop settles it

clip_level.reading: 2.8x the correct marks at the same or slightly lower error rate among marks that could be checked (22% vs 26%). Most wrong marks are one character from a real plate on the same clip; a one-vote read is published as a lead requiring verification, never a confirmation.

final_pipeline.measured: 2026-09-28, same clips, full production pipeline after the 0000/RTO-0 rules, the lookalike-agreement vote (edit distance >= 0.7, share >= 0.4) and weakest-character lead gating
final_pipeline.note: Correct/wrong verdicts are the by-eye audit of the first run's published marks; marks the final pipeline publishes that were not in that run are counted as not settled.
final_pipeline.synthetic_corpus_leads: Of 1,088 valid reads (1,032 real, 56 invented), a mean-confidence bar of 0.82 kept 41 invented reads; a weakest-character bar of 0.82 kept 11 while keeping 852 real. tests/integration/test_pipeline_corpus.py passes 5/5 with the real weights.
